pages.title: What it does
text: Every attack rolls against this percentage independently; on a hit the damage is multiplied by your critical multiplier.
Critical multiplier = 1.5 + critical damage / 100, so with 0 critical damage a crit is the vanilla 1.5x.
The vanilla jump crit uses the same path and is overwritten by the same multiplier.

pages.title: Flat (numeric) line
text: The curve is LINEAR: +0.833333 percentage points per point.
The old curve, gain = 50 * x / (x + 60), had an initial slope of 50/60 = 0.833333, so the early feel is unchanged.

pages.title: Percent line
text: Also LINEAR: 1.25 per point, on the DESIGN_BASELINE basis with reference B_ref = 20 percentage points.
Contribution = 20 * gain / 100, i.e. +0.25 percentage points per point. 20 points -> +5.00; 50 -> +12.50; 100 -> +25.00; 200 -> +50.00.
Because the basis is a fixed number, this line pays out even with no gear at all and can never degenerate to zero.

pages.title: Ceiling & returns
text: The probability ceiling is pinned at 100% (FIXED; it does not follow the attribute range). A probability above 100% means nothing.

Whatever the two lines add up to, anything above 100% is capped by the mod: points are still accepted, the effect stops at 100%, the row shows a "!" marker and /rpg stats reports stat.crit_chance.clamped as true.
The "!" marker has two meanings here: the vanilla attribute range may have truncated the value, or this mod's own functional cap may be biting. Either way, "more points will not help" is shown.

pages.title: Practical advice
text: Critical chance is only meaningful together with critical damage: 20% chance with 0 critical damage is worse than putting those points straight into attack damage.
The usual route is 25%..35% chance first, then everything into critical damage.
Of the two lines the flat one is better at low counts (12.5% for 20 points), while the percent line is the stable one because its basis is fixed.
